claim: Amnesia-type deficits (drug or new learning after training/reactivation) often recover with time, reminders, re-dosing or engram stimulation, so access can be lost while the trace stays. The broad claim of 'most if not all' is advocate-made and unproven.
agent_test: Compare erase-style memory edit vs cue-restore on an old-fact probe at equal tokens.

claim: In mice, light on tagged dentate gyrus engram cells restores freezing after anisomycin amnesia (Ryan 2015, Roy 2017) and restores social recognition memory after sleep deprivation (Sarma 2026); natural cues fail. Rodent only, specific cell populations and stimulation protocols. Dissent: Abdou 2018 found light on auditory inputs to the lateral amygdala failed to induce recall after complete amnesia. Replications are by related labs; strict count unknown.
agent_test: Analogue: test whether a stored note is present but not surfaced by the default retrieval query.
audit_note: Sarma et al. 2026 rescued social recognition memory after sleep deprivation, not freezing; the wording 'restores freezing ... and after sleep loss' wrongly extends the freezing result to a different behavior.
claim_before_audit: In mice, light on tagged dentate gyrus engram cells restores freezing after anisomycin amnesia (Ryan 2015, Roy 2017) and after sleep loss (Sarma 2026); natural cues fail. Rodent only, specific cell populations and stimulation protocols. Dissent: Abdou 2018 found light on auditory inputs failed after complete amnesia. Replications are by related labs; strict count unknown.

claim: Early-Alzheimer mouse models show the same pattern: engram stimulation rescues memory that natural cues cannot reach.
agent_test: No direct test; treat as support for the access-vs-storage split.

claim: Rat reminders or re-giving the amnesic drug reverse cycloheximide and LiCl amnesia (Gisquet-Verrier 2015); the drug-state integration account explains the time gradient. Same lab family as the review.
agent_test: State-matching test: put the same context framing at retrieval as at encoding.

claim: Human reconsolidation-based memory erasure is weak or contested: Walker 2003 failed in four direct replications (N=64, pooled BF01 5.74) and three conceptual ones (N=48).
agent_test: Do not build a reactivate-then-overwrite step expecting clean edits.

claim: Propranolol reconsolidation blockade in humans: Pigeon 2022 g=-0.51 (healthy, 14 studies, n=478) and g=-0.42 (clinical, 12 studies, n=446); Steenen 2022 finds no significant benefit after risk-of-bias restriction; Schiller 2010 re-analysis depends on exclusions; a healthy N=44 replication failed.
agent_test: None for the agent; shows weakness of the main rival, not proof of retrieval failure.

claim: Post-retrieval extinction meta-analysis: humans fear g=0.40, animal appetitive g=0.89, animal fear g=0.21 (ns). Effects are moderated, not universal.
agent_test: none

claim: Retrieval cues work by diagnostic value and match (encoding specificity), not by overlap alone; items missed in free recall are recovered with cues.
agent_test: Cue-design A/B: query in encoding vocabulary vs paraphrase, same token budget.
audit_note: Free-recall-to-cued-recall recovery (Tulving & Pearlstone 1966) is described in the Alfei review; Warrington & Weiskrantz was only read as an abstract and concerns amnesic patients with partial cues.

claim: Retrieval failure is not the whole story for patients: FCSRT cueing separates storage deficits from retrieval deficits; bvFTD stays impaired on cued recall (effect -1.25, 209 vs 235, 8 studies) while free recall is worse (-1.98).
agent_test: Check whether cue rescue fails on facts never stored; control with never-seen facts.

claim: In LLMs, performance lost after fine-tuning is often recoverable cheaply: spurious forgetting task accuracy ~100% to ~10% in 150 steps, recovery probe ~96%; safety 100% to 0% then ~99% after ten refusal examples. The probe is retraining, so it shows savings, not pure cue access.
agent_test: Probe a degraded behaviour with a few examples in context vs weight change; measure recovery at equal tokens.
audit_note: Safety recovery in paper is 'ten epochs on ten safety instances'; second source (Kotha) only supports the general idea that ability remains after fine-tuning.

claim: Unlearned LLM knowledge returns with small unrelated or loosely related data: WMDP-Bio 29.9/29.5/27.9% back to 52.7/57.0/61.6% (RMU/NPO/DPO) with 10 retain samples (base 64.4%); Deeb and Roger recover at least 88% on pretraining-era facts; Hu 2025 benign relearning above 70% keyword success; Who's Harry Potter resurfaces with ~1% corpus.
agent_test: Not an agent test; supports suppressed-is-not-erased. Caveat: fine-tuned-in facts recover less for some methods.

claim: Models encode answers they do not output: internal scorer gap 40% relative; in 9% of questions the true answer ranked first internally though never sampled in 1000 tries; hidden states encode truth but signals do not transfer across datasets. Gap check: probe beats majority vote by about 1.7 points (23.7 vs 22.0) at 1000 samples; cross-dataset transfer is weak after a logit baseline.
agent_test: Add a re-score step over sampled candidates; compare with majority vote at equal tokens.

claim: Retrieval depends on cue direction and form: Reversal Curse (GPT-4 parent 79% vs child 33%; fine-tune 96.7% vs ~0 reversed) and extraction needs varied paraphrase at training (near 0% held-out QA without it); a fact in context removes the curse.
agent_test: Query the memory store in both directions and with paraphrases; count hits at equal tokens.

claim: Position is a cue: multi-document QA accuracy is U-shaped over position and longer context does not fix it (over 20-point drop for GPT-3.5; at 20 and 30 documents below 56.1% closed-book).
agent_test: Place key evidence at start/end of the prompt vs middle.

claim: Proactive interference in LLM context: accuracy on the latest value falls log-linearly toward zero as old updates to the same key accumulate (35 variants); ignore-earlier prompts help little; a fixed-length control keeps the effect.
agent_test: Overwrite stale notes rather than append; compare with append-only at equal tokens.

claim: Deleted information remains in hidden states and can be extracted: white-box attack 38% (budget 20), black-box paraphrase 29% on a GPT-J edited model.
agent_test: none

claim: Agent memory designs act as cue design: recency/relevance/importance scoring (Generative Agents), paging with self-search (MemGPT deep retrieval GPT-4 32.1% to 92.5%), reflection notes (Reflexion), linked tagged notes (A-MEM). Tasks and baselines differ, so results are not comparable.
agent_test: Ablate each retrieval signal on one fixed agent task at equal tokens.

claim: Human cue-induced amnesia from reminders and ECS in people is weak; the review's human evidence is thinner than its rodent evidence.
agent_test: none

claim: No LLM test of cue reinstatement of encoding framing was found. Prompt-only recovery of buried knowledge does exist (adversarial prefix, in-context relearning), but cues are optimised or content-bearing, not a natural framing match. LLM parallels stay by analogy.
agent_test: Design a context-reinstatement test: restore encoding framing and compare recall.

claim: Context change and generalisation matter: midazolam amnesia generalises to a similar context but recovers in the original context (N=32, 24, 48 across experiments); after 27 days the first-learned association dominates (Sissons and Miller).
agent_test: Test stale-vs-recent preference after long gaps in agent memory.

claim: Prompt-only recovery of unlearned LLM knowledge is real but partial: enhanced GCG prefix lifts WMDP-Bio from 29.9/29.5/27.9 to 53.9/46.0/49.0 (base 64.4) and Cyber from 27.7/32.7/33.5 to 35.3/37.0/36.7 (base 42.6); in-context relearning gives modest gains on Harry Potter familiarity.
agent_test: Test a reminder cue (summary in context) against a no-cue prompt on a buried fact.

claim: The Alfei review gives no tally of failed versus successful reversals; Table 1 lists noteworthy positive examples, marks untested cells, and admits no recovery by US reinstatement or state-dependent retrieval was found for proactive or retroactive outcome interference.
agent_test: Do not quote a hit rate for cue-based recovery.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Write-time cue enrichment helps retrieval: adding extracted facts to index keys raised LongMemEval recall@5 from 0.582 to 0.644 (rounds) and 0.706 to 0.732 (sessions), +5.4% QA accuracy on average. Read-side time-aware query expansion adds 6.8 to 11.3% recall but only with a strong rewriter (Llama 8B can hurt).
agent_test: Store a one-line fact key with each note; add a query rewrite only if the model is strong.

claim: Single query rewriting gives 0 to 3 points (Ma 2023: HotpotQA EM 30.47 to 32.80 LLM rewrite; AmbigNQ 45.80 to 46.40) and no paper found compares multi-paraphrase or reverse-direction re-querying with one query at equal tokens (gap 3 open). On LoCoMo a compact store (Mem0 66.88 J at 1764 tokens) beats chunk RAG (best 60.97) but not full context (72.90 at 26031 tokens); no state-matching test exists (gap 8 open).
agent_test: Run own A/B: one query vs three paraphrases at matched token budget.

claim: Overwrite versus append against proactive interference is untested at equal tokens. Telling the model to forget old values gains under 10 points at 100 updates; a mock QA reset helps most (Gemini Flash 2.0 at 150 updates matches baseline at 30-45).
agent_test: Test deleting stale notes from context against appending with a 'latest wins' rule.

claim: A feeling-of-knowing analogue exists for LLMs but needs training or hidden states: P(IK) AUROC 0.864 on TriviaQA (52B), and when trained on TriviaQA only 0.606 to 0.687 on LAMBADA, Python and GSM8K (0.928 on Mixed-Arithmetic); probes on exact-answer tokens give AUC 0.83 to 0.95 but do not transfer across datasets once a logit baseline is subtracted.
agent_test: Cheap proxy for an API agent: agreement across paraphrased queries (untested).
audit_note: Kadavath et al. Table 1 shows trained-on-TriviaQA P(IK) AUROC out of distribution of 0.606 (LAMBADA), 0.687 (Python), 0.624 (GSM8K) but 0.928 on Mixed-Arithmetic, so the stated 0.606-0.687 range omits the strongest transfer case.
claim_before_audit: A feeling-of-knowing analogue exists for LLMs but needs training or hidden states: P(IK) AUROC 0.864 on TriviaQA (52B), 0.606 to 0.687 out of distribution when trained on TriviaQA only; probes on exact-answer tokens give AUC 0.83 to 0.95 but do not transfer across datasets once a logit baseline is subtracted.

claim: Human cue-induced effects that work depend on conditions: a reminder raised intrusions of new items into old recall (Hupbach 2007, groups of 12, U=20, p<0.01) without changing correct recall; propranolol erasure (Kindt 2009) has mixed replication; Steenen's restricted pooled propranolol effect is only in forest plots (gap 7 open).
agent_test: A reminder can contaminate old content with new; keep source tags.
